reports.rendered_content: Normal graybox implementation has been upgraded from occlusion foundation to a full algorithm with 17 coverage-engine files, worker, UI, and tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. Key strengths: deterministic surface sampler using barycentric coordinates weighted by world-space area; origin evaluation includes actual segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility and usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values; shared coarse-to-fine engine with 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, and separate fixed-first and joint branches; tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Two critical blockers remain: (1) imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because clearance uses entire object AABBs—any camera origin inside an object's AABB gets zero clearance and is rejected, affecting complete Maya sets, room shells, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, and large models with empty interior space; fix requires actual geometry clearance via point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast through coverage BVH, with per-connected-mesh or spatial-cluster obstacle bounds rather than per-imported-set-object; (2) geometry representation does not scale to heavy imports (content truncated).
